text: Grok ByAPI 是面向 DSH Web 的 Grok 模型接入插件，通过可配置的 OpenAI 兼容网关注册聊天模型，并按能力发现和分类模型。它还提供图片生成与编辑、视频生成/编辑/延长、文本转语音工具；媒体任务和生成文件保存到本机，并可在会话中查看任务状态。设置页可配置网关地址、密钥、超时和各类模型。使用前需要网关地址及调用密钥；模型和媒体请求会发送至该网关。

Grok ByAPI connects DSH Web to Grok chat through a compatible gateway. It discovers models and provides tools for image and video creation and editing, video extension, and text-to-speech. Media tasks and files are saved locally. Configure a gateway and API key; requests go there.

Grok ByAPI 的功能「Grok 聊天模型接入」：在模型发现后把所选 chat 类模型注册到 DSH 的模型路由，供模型选择器调用。可配置兼容网关及 API 协议。
Grok ByAPI 的功能「图片生成与编辑」：通过工具按提示生成图片，也可提供 1–5 张参考图或已保存图片任务进行编辑；结果保存为本地文件。
Grok ByAPI 的功能「视频与语音媒体工具」：工具可生成、编辑或延长视频，也可把文本合成为 MP3；任务状态和已保存结果可查询。

Grok ByAPI README · dsh-grok-byapi：One plugin, one gateway connection. Chat models appear in the model picker; image, video, and TTS models stay out of it and are used through tools instead. Any chat model — Grok or another provider — can call those tools. The plugin talks to a Grok gateway you already run (CLIProxyAPI by default), keeps the API key in the dsh credential service, and saves generated media locally. It is not an OAuth client, does not provide an account or quota, and does not read the Grok CLI OAuth token.

Grok ByAPI README · Features：| Area | Current scope |
| --- | --- |
| Chat provider | Registers a native dsh LLM provider: route `xAI-CLIProxyAPI`, display name **Grok**. Streaming text and tool calls go through the official pi-ai adapter. |
| Model catalog | `GET /models` discovery, auto-categorized as chat, image, video, speech, research, or unknown. Only chat models enter the picker; unknown models do not. Per-model overrides are available. |
| Settings page | Connection, API key, verification, timeout, the chat-model table (the picker's source of truth), and media-model selection. Copy follows the dsh language (English or Chinese). |
| Durable media tasks | Task records are per session and survive restarts. Downloads write `.part` files and are renamed after validation. Storage is isolated by connection and task. |
| Results in chat | Tool result cards, file preview, and a sidebar player for MP4, MP3, and WAV. Tool cards and the player follow the dsh language. |

Grok ByAPI README · Features：Together, the plugin's two components register 10 tools. The plugin page has connection and model settings only. The grok-byapi detail lists chat and the catalog; the dsh-grok-imagine detail lists image, video, and speech:

Grok ByAPI README · Features：| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `grok_models` | Refreshes the catalog and returns models grouped by capability. Optional `verify_key` checks address and key with one `GET /models`. |
| `grok_generate_image` | Text to image: `prompt`, optional `model`, `n` (1–4, default 1). |
| `grok_edit_image` | Image to image: `prompt` plus `image_url` / `image_urls` (up to 5) or a saved image task. |
| `grok_generate_video` | Text to video, or image to video when one still (`image_url` or a saved image task) is attached. `duration` is 1–15 seconds, default 2. |
| `grok_edit_video` | Video to video: edit an existing video from a prompt (`video_url` or a saved video task). |
| `grok_extend_video` | Continues from the last frame and joins that to the original clip. |
| `grok_speak` | Text to speech saved as MP3: `input`, optional `model` and `voice`. |
| `grok_media_list` | Lists media tasks created in the current session. |
| `grok_media_status` | Checks a task and downloads the result when ready: `task_id`. |
| `grok_media_retry_download` | Retries a failed download without regenerating: `task_id`. |

Grok ByAPI README · Features：Not provided: speech recognition, realtime voice, direct OAuth, and a live task dashboard. Video jobs are polled in-process after submit, but the result card does not refresh itself. Classification is rule-based, not a guarantee.

Grok ByAPI README · Compatibility：`engines.dsh` is the compatibility gate; `peerDependencies` pin the SDK packages the source uses but do not decide compatibility, so rerun the integration tests after a dsh upgrade. A direct xAI or other compatible endpoint can serve chat, but image, video, and TTS need the gateway to expose the matching Grok endpoints.

Grok ByAPI README · Update and uninstall：Removing the plugin takes its layer out of the profile: the provider, the 10 tools, and its settings page are gone. Generated media and task records are not deleted — remove the data directory yourself if you want them gone. A credential created for the plugin is also not removed by uninstall; delete it in dsh if you no longer need it.

Grok ByAPI README · Configuration：| Key | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `connection.baseURL` | `http://127.0.0.1:8317/v1` | Gateway base URL. `127.0.0.1` is the machine running dsh; use your own HTTPS URL for a remote gateway. |

| `connection.verify` | `true` | Verify `GET /models` with the saved key when settings are saved. |
| `connection.timeoutMs` | `60000` | Request timeout in milliseconds (1000–600000). |
| `media.imageModel` | empty | Image model used when a call omits `model`. |
| `media.videoModel` | empty | Video model used when a call omits `model`. |
| `media.speechModel` | empty | TTS model used when a call omits `model`. |
| `media.dataDir` | empty | Media output directory; empty means `$DSH_HOME/plugins/dsh-grok-byapi`. |
| `modelOverrides` | `[]` | Per-model overrides written by the settings page: category, display na

Grok ByAPI README · Configuration：The settings page writes the API key into the dsh credential service under the reference name above; the configuration keeps only the reference. Do not hand-write a key into YAML. The media model IDs in the example come from the test gateway — run `grok_models` and use the IDs your gateway reports.

Grok ByAPI README · Security and privacy：- **Network:** only the gateway you configure. Discovery calls `GET /models`, chat uses the configured OpenAI-compatible route, and media tools call image, video, and TTS endpoints on the same base URL. No telemetry.
- **Credentials:** the key lives in the dsh credential service; it is not written to YAML, logs, task records, or the repository. Third-party media downloads are requested without the gateway key.
- **Files:** generated media goes to `$DSH_HOME/plugins/dsh-grok-byapi` (or `media.dataDir`). Task records may contain signed upstream URLs; treat them as private.
- **Not done by this plugin:** reading or reusing the Grok CLI OAuth token, installing or running other plugins, fetching runtime dependencies at install time.

Grok ByAPI README · Security and privacy：Installing any dsh plugin runs third-party code with your user permissions, and tool approvals do not sandbox plugin code — review the source before installing. Please report security issues through [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

Grok ByAPI README · Usage：- **Chat:** choose **Grok** in the model picker. Only chat models are listed; the settings page's model table is what the picker shows, so delete a row and save to hide that model.
- **Images:** one call generates and saves; inline the result with an absolute local path — ``. dsh Web serves it through `/api/file`; the limit is 20 MiB per file.
- **Video:** submits a job (1–15 s). Call `grok_media_status` with the returned `task_id` until `saved` or `failed`; `submission-unknown` means do not submit again. There is no automatic polling or completion notification.
- **Speech:** `grok_speak` writes an MP3; `grok_media_retry_download` retries only the download and never regenerates.
- **Display:** video and audio appear in the tool result card player. Do not inline them with Markdown image syntax — the chat does not render them and shows a broken image instead.

Grok ByAPI README · Troubleshooting：Installation is successful when all four checks pass:

1. `dsh --profile grok-byapi-test --dump-config` lists the `grok-byapi` layer.
2. The Plugins page shows this plugin with both components (the provider and `dsh-grok-imagine`) running.
3. `grok_models` returns categorized model IDs.
4. After `dsh plugin --profile grok-byapi-test remove dsh-grok-byapi`, the layer and components are gone.

Grok ByAPI README · Troubleshooting：| Symptom | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `dsh plugin add` fails or reports 404 | Install `dsh-grok-byapi@0.2.1` from npm, or use the git / tarball path above. |
| Plugin is listed but does not load | Your dsh is outside `>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0-0`. Upgrade to a 0.2.x build. |
| 401 or 403 in settings | Wrong key or base URL. Re-save the key and check the `/v1` suffix. |
| Connection refused or timeout | Gateway not running or unreachable; `127.0.0.1` means the dsh host. |
| No Grok models in the picker | `/models` returned nothing classified as chat; refresh `grok_models` and add overrides. |
| Model not discovered or wrong category | Refresh `grok_models`, then correct the category in the settings page. |
| Image, video, or TTS fails while chat works | The gateway does not expose the matching Grok endpoints; the plugin cannot add them. |
| Video stays generating | Query `grok_media_status`; do not resubmit a `submission-unknown` task. |

Grok ByAPI README · Development：CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs on Linux and Windows with Node 22.19 and 24: install, tests, syntax checks, build, a check that `lib/client.js` matches the build output, and a pack dry run. Pushing a `v*` tag runs `.github/workflows/release.yml`, which verifies that the tag matches `package.json`, repeats the checks, attaches the packed tarball to a GitHub Release, and publishes to npm through trusted publishing (OIDC) — the workflow holds no npm token. The package is published on npm (`0.2.1` is the current `latest`), and every release is available there as well as from git/tarball. See [Publishing](#publishing) for the one-time npmjs.com registration and for publishing from your own machine. See [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md) for planned work and [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) for changes.

Grok ByAPI README · Publishing：CI publishes to npm with trusted publishing (OIDC). The workflow stores no npm token: GitHub hands the runner a short-lived OIDC token and npm exchanges it for a publish token, so there is no long-lived secret to keep or leak.

Register the trusted publisher once, in npmjs.com → the package → Settings → Trusted publishing:

Grok ByAPI README · Publishing：| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Organization or user | `NingYuanLee` |
| Repository | `dsh-grok-byapi` |
| Workflow filename | `release.yml` — the file name only, including `.yml`, matched case-sensitively |
| Environment name | leave empty |

npm 11.16 and newer can register the same relationship from the command line (run `npm login` first):

```bash
npm trust github dsh-grok-byapi --file release.yml --repo NingYuanLee/dsh-grok-byapi --allow-publish
```

Grok ByAPI README · Publishing：Publishing from your own machine follows npm's official local flow: log in through the browser for a session token that is valid for two hours, then publish with the one-time code from your authenticator.

```bash
npm login --auth-type=web
npm publish --otp <code>
```

Grok ByAPI README · Publishing：Keep every token and one-time code out of the repository, logs, and commit messages. npm does not verify a trusted publisher registration when it is saved: a wrong repository or workflow filename only surfaces at publish time as `ENEEDAUTH`.

| `grok_media_list` | Lists media tasks created in the current session. |

Grok ByAPI README · dsh-grok-byapi：One plugin, one gateway connection. Chat models appear in the model picker; image, video, and TTS models stay out of it and are used through tools instead. Any chat model — Grok or another provider — can call those tools. The plugin talks to a Grok gateway you already run (CLIProxyAPI by default), keeps the API key in the dsh credential service, and saves generated media locally. It is not an OAuth client, does not provide an account or quota, and does not read the Grok CLI OAuth token.

Grok ByAPI README · Features：| Area | Current scope |
| --- | --- |
| Chat provider | Registers a native dsh LLM provider: route `xAI-CLIProxyAPI`, display name **Grok**. Streaming text and tool calls go through the official pi-ai adapter. |
| Model catalog | `GET /models` discovery, auto-categorized as chat, image, video, speech, research, or unknown. Only chat models enter the picker; unknown models do not. Per-model overrides are available. |
| Settings page | Connection, API key, verification, timeout, the chat-model table (the picker's source of truth), and media-model selection. Copy follows the dsh language (English or Chinese). |
| Durable media tasks | Task records are per session and survive restarts. Downloads write `.part` files and are renamed after validation. Storage is isolated by connection and task. |
| Results in chat | Tool result cards, file preview, and a sidebar player for MP4, MP3, and WAV. Tool cards and the player follow the dsh language. |

| `grok_models` | Refreshes the catalog and returns models grouped by capability. Optional `verify_key` checks address and key with one `GET /models`. |

| `grok_edit_image` | Image to image: `prompt` plus `image_url` / `image_urls` (up to 5) or a saved image task. |
| `grok_generate_video` | Text to video, or image to video when one still (`image_url` or a saved image task) is attached. `duration` is 1–15 seconds, default 2. |
| `grok_edit_video` | Video to video: edit an existing video from a prompt (`video_url` or a saved video task). |
| `grok_extend_video` | Continues from the last frame and joins that to the original clip. |

Grok ByAPI README · Security and privacy：- **Network:** only the gateway you configure. Discovery calls `GET /models`, chat uses the configured OpenAI-compatible route, and media tools call image, video, and TTS endpoints on the same base URL. No telemetry.
- **Credentials:** the key lives in the dsh credential service; it is not written to YAML, logs, task records, or the repository. Third-party media downloads are requested without the gateway key.
- **Files:** generated media goes to `$DSH_HOME/plugins/dsh-grok-byapi` (or `media.dataDir`). Task records may contain signed upstream URLs; treat them as private.
- **Not done by this plugin:** reading or reusing the Grok CLI OAuth token, installing or running other plugins, fetching runtime dependencies at install time.

Grok ByAPI README · Security and privacy：Installing any dsh plugin runs third-party code with your user permissions, and tool approvals do not sandbox plugin code — review the source before installing. Please report security issues through [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

Grok ByAPI README · Usage：- **Chat:** choose **Grok** in the model picker. Only chat models are listed; the settings page's model table is what the picker shows, so delete a row and save to hide that model.
- **Images:** one call generates and saves; inline the result with an absolute local path — ``. dsh Web serves it through `/api/file`; the limit is 20 MiB per file.
- **Video:** submits a job (1–15 s). Call `grok_media_status` with the returned `task_id` until `saved` or `failed`; `submission-unknown` means do not submit again. There is no automatic polling or completion notification.
- **Speech:** `grok_speak` writes an MP3; `grok_media_retry_download` retries only the download and never regenerates.
- **Display:** video and audio appear in the tool result card player. Do not inline them with Markdown image syntax — the chat does not render them and shows a broken image instead.

Grok ByAPI README · Troubleshooting：Installation is successful when all four checks pass:

1. `dsh --profile grok-byapi-test --dump-config` lists the `grok-byapi` layer.
2. The Plugins page shows this plugin with both components (the provider and `dsh-grok-imagine`) running.
3. `grok_models` returns categorized model IDs.
4. After `dsh plugin --profile grok-byapi-test remove dsh-grok-byapi`, the layer and components are gone.

Grok ByAPI README · Troubleshooting：| Symptom | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `dsh plugin add` fails or reports 404 | Install `dsh-grok-byapi@0.2.1` from npm, or use the git / tarball path above. |
| Plugin is listed but does not load | Your dsh is outside `>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0-0`. Upgrade to a 0.2.x build. |
| 401 or 403 in settings | Wrong key or base URL. Re-save the key and check the `/v1` suffix. |
| Connection refused or timeout | Gateway not running or unreachable; `127.0.0.1` means the dsh host. |
| No Grok models in the picker | `/models` returned nothing classified as chat; refresh `grok_models` and add overrides. |
| Model not discovered or wrong category | Refresh `grok_models`, then correct the category in the settings page. |
| Image, video, or TTS fails while chat works | The gateway does not expose the matching Grok endpoints; the plugin cannot add them. |
| Video stays generating | Query `grok_media_status`; do not resubmit a `submission-unknown` task. |

Grok ByAPI README · Publishing：CI publishes to npm with trusted publishing (OIDC). The workflow stores no npm token: GitHub hands the runner a short-lived OIDC token and npm exchanges it for a publish token, so there is no long-lived secret to keep or leak.

Register the trusted publisher once, in npmjs.com → the package → Settings → Trusted publishing:

Grok ByAPI README · Publishing：| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Organization or user | `NingYuanLee` |
| Repository | `dsh-grok-byapi` |
| Workflow filename | `release.yml` — the file name only, including `.yml`, matched case-sensitively |
| Environment name | leave empty |

npm 11.16 and newer can register the same relationship from the command line (run `npm login` first):

```bash
npm trust github dsh-grok-byapi --file release.yml --repo NingYuanLee/dsh-grok-byapi --allow-publish
```

Grok ByAPI README · Publishing：Publishing from your own machine follows npm's official local flow: log in through the browser for a session token that is valid for two hours, then publish with the one-time code from your authenticator.

```bash
npm login --auth-type=web
npm publish --otp <code>
```

Grok ByAPI README · Publishing：Keep every token and one-time code out of the repository, logs, and commit messages. npm does not verify a trusted publisher registration when it is saved: a wrong repository or workflow filename only surfaces at publish time as `ENEEDAUTH`.
